claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, debugging was frustrating due to CloudFormation templates, and multi-cloud was nearly impossible.
SST was originally built on top of AWS CDK, which allowed developers to define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.

AWS CDK is AWS-only, while Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem; Pulumi supports any programming language while CDK supports TypeScript and Python; CDK is slower due to CloudFormation while Pulumi has faster direct execution; CDK uses a CloudFormation state file while Pulumi manages state; CDK secrets management is AWS Secrets Manager only while Pulumi supports cross-cloud secrets.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine while also bridging Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.

The Founding Engineer at SST said: 'With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle.'
With CDK and CloudFormation, infrastructure code produces an intermediary format (YAML or JSON) that is then executed to deploy resources.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make the underlying cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud dependency; the Pulumi engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST keeps its deployment state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than in Pulumi Cloud.
Nitric and Defang also run application deployments through the Pulumi engine rather than building their own diff, state, and provider layer.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying applications to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST users define infrastructure and code together in a single `sst.config.ts` file using SST components.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation.
In late 2023 the SST team began a rewrite code-named Ion that replaced the entire deployment layer.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN)."

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources."
SST docs 'What is SST' say: "SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi."
Gautier Blandin writes in 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' that SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST's constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka writes in 'SST ditches AWS CDK. Time to move on to Ion': "You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now."
SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi plus first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and others, and the @pulumiverse/vercel provider.
In SST's deploy chain, the Pulumi engine diffs desired vs actual state, builds a dependency graph and orders operations, and Pulumi's Terraform bridge translates resources into cloud API calls.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
Pulumi users can consume Terraform providers directly via the provider bridge.
Nitric's docs state "all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments," with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's Pulumi provider takes "a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`" to provision the result.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state; its Terraform providers are bridged through the Pulumi engine.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode now has a larger GitHub following (star count) than SST itself.
The SST repository is anomalyco/sst (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi offers Pulumi Cloud for cross-team visibility, policy as code for central guardrails, and components for sharing infrastructure patterns.
